utilityName: City of Mansfield Water Utilities Backflow Testing
testingFrequency: Upon installation, repair, or relocation; annual testing expected for assemblies
dueBasis: Mansfield says all backflow protection assemblies must be tested upon installation, repair, or relocation and that assemblies should be tested annually to ensure they are working.
coveredPropertyTypes: Properties requiring licensed backflow inspector reporting
officialListLabel: Search Mansfield licensed backflow inspectors through VEPO

submissionMethods.label: Mansfield Water Utilities backflow testing page

penalties: Mansfield routes accepted reporting through the online VEPO system and adds testers to the approved list only after license, insurance, and test accuracy verification.
sourceExcerpt: Mansfield publishes installation, repair, relocation, and annual testing language, then sends tester submission and licensed inspector lookup through VEPO.
verdictSummary: Mansfield is a source-backed VEPO city because its public Water Utilities page connects annual/device testing, licensed inspector lookup, online VEPO submission, and verified tester approval.
whoIsAffected: Mansfield properties with backflow prevention assemblies, especially installations, repairs, relocations, annual test cycles, and fire protection sprinkler assemblies.
residentialNotes: Residential impact usually appears when a tracked assembly is installed, repaired, relocated, or due for annual testing.
Use the licensed inspector route instead of a generic search when the City workflow matters.
commercialNotes: Commercial owners need a licensed inspector who can use Mansfield's VEPO reporting path.
Fire sprinkler assemblies need a qualified BPAT tied to a licensed fire protection sprinkler company.

annualTesting.summary: Mansfield states assemblies should be tested annually and also tested on installation, repair, or relocation.
highlights: Installation, repair, and relocation are also testing triggers.
VEPO controls the online test report workflow.
workflowSteps: Confirm the Mansfield assembly and annual or event trigger.
Use a licensed backflow inspector in the VEPO route.
Have the tester submit through Mansfield's online VEPO workflow.

irrigation.summary: Mansfield's public page describes irrigation as a backflow risk example, so irrigation users should verify whether the assembly is tracked and due under the same VEPO workflow.
highlights: Irrigation is identified as a potential backflow source.
Assembly status controls whether the test is due.
Licensed inspector lookup is still the practical route.
workflowSteps: Confirm whether the irrigation assembly is tracked by Mansfield.
Use the VEPO licensed inspector route.
Keep the submission tied to the correct assembly record.

fireLine.summary: Mansfield repeats the State Fire Marshal constraint for fire protection sprinkler assemblies.
highlights: Fire protection sprinkler assemblies are separately called out.
A BPAT must be a full-time employee of a licensed fire protection sprinkler company.
VEPO portal access still matters for the report path.
workflowSteps: Check whether the assembly is tied to a fire sprinkler system.
Use a BPAT who satisfies the fire sprinkler employment rule.
Submit through the Mansfield VEPO route.
Open Mansfield's official backflow testing page.
Use the VEPO route to find a licensed inspector.
Have the tester submit through the online password-protected VEPO system.
Verify fire sprinkler or annual constraints before treating the report as complete.
failureHighlights: A tester must be verified for license, insurance, and test accuracy before approved-list addition.
The online VEPO submission path is the practical acceptance point.
Fire sprinkler assemblies require the State Fire Marshal employment overlay.

costBand.testingRange: Private Mansfield pricing varies by assembly and access.
